subject: Political Science (Code: 323)
past_paper_reference: CUET UG Political Science Past Papers (2022-2024)

questions.question: In the first general elections of 1952, the Indian National Congress won 74% of the Lok Sabha seats by securing approximately what percentage of the total popular vote?
questions.explanation: The Congress won 364 out of 489 seats (74.4%) with 45% of the popular vote, benefiting from the first-past-the-post electoral system where opposition votes were split.

questions.question: During the accession crisis of 1947, the hereditary ruler of Hyderabad was designated as the Nizam, whereas the ruler of Junagadh was titled the:
questions.explanation: The ruler of the princely state of Junagadh in Saurashtra was Nawab Mahabat Khan III, while Hyderabad was ruled by Nizam Mir Osman Ali Khan.

questions.question: Professor P.C. Mahalanobis served as an influential member of the Planning Commission of India for over a decade during which period?
questions.explanation: P.C. Mahalanobis was appointed as a member of the Planning Commission in 1955 and continued until 1967, directing the formulation of industrial planning strategy.

questions.question: The armed border skirmishes between India and Pakistan in April 1965, prior to the full-scale war in September, took place in the salt marshlands of:
options: A) The Thar Desert in Rajasthan
B) The Sunderbans in West Bengal
C) The Kargil heights in Ladakh
D) The Rann of Kutch in Gujarat
questions.explanation: Pakistani troops crossed the international border in the Rann of Kutch in Gujarat in April 1965, claiming sovereign jurisdiction over the northern half of the salt marshes.

questions.topic: Challenge to and Restoration of Congress System
questions.question: In the landmark 1971 general elections, Indira Gandhi's Congress (R) formed a national electoral alliance with which prominent leftist party?
questions.explanation: Congress (R) forged an electoral pact with the CPI, which won 23 seats, endorsing Indira Gandhi's socialist platform and foreign policy tilt towards the USSR.

questions.question: The sixth general elections that brought an end to the National Emergency and resulted in the defeat of the Congress party were held in which month and year?
questions.explanation: The historic general elections were conducted in March 1977 after Indira Gandhi unexpectedly released political detainees and called for polls in January.

questions.question: Operation Blue Star, the military assault on the Golden Temple complex in Amritsar in June 1984, was ordered by which Prime Minister of India?
questions.explanation: Prime Minister Indira Gandhi authorized the military action Operation Blue Star in early June 1984 to flush out armed extremists barricaded inside the Golden Temple.

questions.question: Which dedicated social activist emerged as the foremost leader of the Narmada Bachao Andolan, championing environmental justice and rehabilitation for displaced adivasis?
questions.explanation: Medha Patkar founded the Narmada Bachao Andolan in 1989, mobilizing displaced tribal communities, farmers, and environmentalists through non-violent satyagraha.

questions.question: Under which Article of the Constitution of India was the Second Backward Classes Commission (Mandal Commission) officially appointed by the President in 1979?
questions.explanation: Article 340 of the Indian Constitution empowers the President to appoint a commission to investigate the conditions of socially and educationally backward classes.

questions.question: The 104th Constitutional Amendment Act (2020) extended the reservation of seats for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes in the Lok Sabha and State Legislative Assemblies for an additional:
questions.explanation: Enacted in January 2020, the 104th Amendment extended political reservation for SCs and STs up to 25 January 2030, while discontinuing the reserved seats for Anglo-Indians.

questions.topic: Cold War Era and Non-aligned Movement
questions.question: The Marshall Plan, initiated by the United States in 1948 to rebuild war-torn Western Europe, was officially titled the:
questions.explanation: The official legislative name of the Marshall Plan was the 'European Recovery Program' (ERP), signed into law by President Harry Truman in April 1948.

questions.question: In March 1985, who was appointed as the General Secretary of the Communist Party of the Soviet Union (CPSU), initiating sweeping reform policies?
questions.explanation: Mikhail Gorbachev was elected General Secretary of the CPSU on 11 March 1985 following the death of Konstantin Chernenko.

questions.question: Launched by the United States in October 2001 following the September 11 terrorist attacks, Operation Enduring Freedom specifically targeted:
options: A) The Taliban regime and Al-Qaeda in Afghanistan
B) Saddam Hussein's armed forces in Iraq
C) Serbian paramilitary units in Kosovo
D) Somali warlord militias in Mogadishu
questions.explanation: Operation Enduring Freedom was initiated by the US and allied forces against the Taliban government in Afghanistan for harboring Osama bin Laden and Al-Qaeda.

questions.question: The Single European Market, ensuring the free movement of goods, services, capital, and persons, was formally launched across the European Community on:
questions.explanation: The European Single Market came into legal effect on 1 January 1993 pursuant to the provisions of the 1986 Single European Act.

questions.question: In July 1995, which socialist Southeast Asian nation formally became the seventh member of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN)?
questions.explanation: Vietnam joined ASEAN on 28 July 1995, symbolizing historic regional reconciliation following decades of Cold War conflict in Indochina.

questions.question: In June 2017, both India and Pakistan became full-fledged member states of which Eurasian regional security grouping at its Astana Summit?
options: A) Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN)
questions.explanation: India and Pakistan were formally admitted as full members of the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) at the summit held in Astana, Kazakhstan, in June 2017.

questions.question: The regular annual session of the United Nations General Assembly opens every year in which month at the UN headquarters in New York?
questions.explanation: The UN General Assembly gathers annually for its regular session starting on the third Tuesday of September, opening with the high-level General Debate.

questions.question: How many judges serve on the International Court of Justice (ICJ) in The Hague, elected to nine-year terms of office?
questions.explanation: The ICJ consists of 15 judges elected for 9-year terms by the United Nations General Assembly and the Security Council voting concurrently.

questions.question: In non-traditional security discourse, the concept of 'Global Security' emerged in the 1990s to describe challenges that require planetary cooperation, such as:
options: A) Cross-border smuggling of fresh fruit between two adjacent districts
B) Disputes over individual municipal boundary zoning markers
C) Global warming, ozone depletion, international terrorism, and pandemics
D) The routine maintenance of suburban civilian highways
questions.explanation: Global security addresses global planetary threats (climate catastrophe, epidemics, international terrorism) that affect all humanity and cannot be solved by any state alone.

questions.question: The Brundtland Commission that published the seminal 1987 report 'Our Common Future' was officially created by the UN General Assembly under the name:
options: A) Intergovernmental Commission on Global Warming
B) United Nations Environmental Defense Assembly
C) International Council for Planetary Resources
D) World Commission on Environment and Development (WCED)
questions.explanation: The UN General Assembly established the World Commission on Environment and Development (WCED) in 1983, chaired by Gro Harlem Brundtland of Norway.

questions.question: The JVP Committee (Jawaharlal Nehru, Vallabhbhai Patel, and Pattabhi Sitaramayya) appointed by the Congress in December 1948 submitted its report in April 1949, advising:
options: A) Postponing the creation of linguistic states for some years to preserve national unity and economic stability
B) The immediate and unconditional reorganisation of all provinces on mother-tongue lines
C) The transfer of all state reorganisation decisions to the British Commonwealth Secretariat
D) The total abolition of all state governments in favor of a unitary centralized regime
questions.explanation: The JVP report cautioned that while linguistic provinces had emotional support, the priority in the aftermath of Partition must be national security, unity, and economic consolidation.

questions.question: In the 1957 Kerala Legislative Assembly elections, how did the Communist Party of India (CPI) secure a legislative majority to form government?
options: A) It won all 126 seats in a complete clean sweep.
B) It won 60 out of 126 seats and secured the support of five independent legislators.
C) It formed a post-poll coalition with the Bharatiya Jana Sangh.
D) It won 20 seats and was invited by the Governor under discretionary rule.
questions.explanation: The CPI won 60 seats and had the pledged support of 5 independent MLAs, giving it 65 seats in the 126-member House to form the government under E.M.S. Namboodiripad.

questions.question: On 2 October 1952, independent India launched its first massive nationwide rural reconstruction initiative aimed at self-help and village development, titled the:
questions.explanation: The Community Development Programme (CDP) was inaugurated on Gandhi Jayanti (2 October 1952) covering 55 community projects across India to develop agriculture, roads, and village welfare.

questions.question: In 1950, Chinese military forces occupied Tibet, leading to the signing of which agreement in May 1951 affirming Chinese sovereignty while ostensibly guaranteeing Tibetan autonomy?
questions.explanation: Tibetan delegates were pressured into signing the Seventeen Point Agreement on 23 May 1951 in Beijing, which affirmed China's sovereignty over Tibet while guaranteeing internal autonomy.

questions.topic: Challenge to and Restoration of Congress System
questions.question: The formal institutional split in the Indian National Congress in November 1969 was finalized when Congress President S. Nijalingappa:
options: A) Expelled Prime Minister Indira Gandhi from the primary membership of the party for indiscipline
B) Resigned from politics and appointed Indira Gandhi as party president
C) Dissolved the Congress Working Committee and merged with the Swatantra Party
D) Surrendered the party's bank accounts to the Election Commission of India
questions.explanation: On 12 November 1969, Congress President S. Nijalingappa issued an order expelling Prime Minister Indira Gandhi from the Congress party, precipitating the split into Congress (O) and Congress (R).

questions.question: During the Emergency, socialist leader George Fernandes was arrested in June 1976 and tried on conspiracy charges for allegedly transporting explosives to blow up government installations in the:
questions.explanation: George Fernandes was charged with procuring dynamite from Baroda to blow up railway tracks and government buildings in protest against the Emergency.

questions.question: In November 1986, an electoral alliance was forged between the Congress and the National Conference through an accord signed by Prime Minister Rajiv Gandhi and:
questions.explanation: The Rajiv Gandhi-Farooq Abdullah Accord formed an electoral coalition for the March 1987 assembly elections, though widespread allegations of rigging in those polls later fed separatist insurgency.

questions.question: In October 1988, the Bharatiya Kisan Union (BKU) demonstrated its massive agrarian mobilising capacity by paralyzing the central administrative heart of New Delhi with a week-long sit-in at the:
options: D) Boat Club lawns on Rajpath
questions.explanation: Led by Mahendra Singh Tikait, nearly five lakh farmers camped out on the Boat Club lawns on Rajpath in October 1988, forcing the Rajiv Gandhi government to concede their demands.

questions.question: The 'Gujral Doctrine', formulated by External Affairs Minister I.K. Gujral in 1996 to guide India's relations with South Asian neighbors, rested on the fundamental premise of:
options: A) Non-reciprocity, whereby India gives unilateral concessions to its smaller neighbors in good faith without expecting immediate reciprocity.
B) Immediate military intervention in the domestic political affairs of neighboring states.
C) Demanding dollar-for-dollar tariff retaliation against all regional partners.
D) Severing all diplomatic ties with any country bordering the Indian Ocean.
questions.explanation: The Gujral Doctrine recognized that as the largest power, India should conduct diplomacy with neighbors (except Pakistan) on a unilateral non-reciprocal basis of generosity and trust.

questions.question: The 16th Lok Sabha elections in May 2014 marked a decisive turning point in Indian political history because:
options: A) The Indian National Congress won more than 400 seats.
B) A single political party (the BJP) won an absolute majority on its own (282 seats) for the first time in thirty years.
C) The Left Front formed the Union Government with regional support.
D) No single party secured more than 50 seats in the Lok Sabha.
questions.explanation: The BJP's victory in 2014 (winning 282 seats) was the first time since Rajiv Gandhi's 1984 victory that a single political party achieved an absolute parliamentary majority.

questions.topic: Cold War Era and Non-aligned Movement
questions.question: The Warsaw Pact, established by the Soviet Union in May 1955 to bind Eastern European communist states into a mutual defense alliance, was officially dissolved in July 1991 in:
questions.explanation: Leaders of the Warsaw Pact member countries met in Prague on 1 July 1991 to sign the protocol terminating the 36-year-old military alliance.

questions.question: In October 1993, a violent constitutional showdown erupted in Moscow between President Boris Yeltsin and the Russian Parliament (Supreme Soviet), culminating in:
options: A) The unconditional reinstatement of Mikhail Gorbachev as President
B) The deployment of United Nations peacekeepers to disarm Russian forces
C) The permanent relocation of the Russian capital from Moscow to Vladivostok
D) Tanks firing shells at the Russian White House (Parliament building) on Yeltsin's orders to crush legislative resistance
questions.explanation: Yeltsin unconstitutionally dissolved the Supreme Soviet, which retaliated by impeaching him; Yeltsin called in the army, and tanks shelled the White House on 4 October 1993, consolidating executive presidency.

questions.question: During the presidency of Bill Clinton (1993-2001), United States foreign policy pivoted from traditional hard military conflicts towards:
options: A) 'Soft issues' such as democracy promotion, ecological preservation, and international trade expansion
B) Direct territorial annexation of Caribbean islands
C) Total withdrawal of US membership from the United Nations
D) Compulsory military conscription for foreign trade workers
questions.explanation: President Bill Clinton de-emphasized grand military interventions, concentrating instead on global trade agreements (NAFTA, WTO), environmental regimes, and human rights advocacy.

questions.question: The European integration process was inaugurated in April 1951 when France, West Germany, Italy, Belgium, the Netherlands, and Luxembourg signed the Treaty of Paris, establishing the:
options: B) European Coal and Steel Community (ECSC)
questions.explanation: The 1951 Treaty of Paris pooled French and German coal and steel production under a common High Authority, making war between them materially impossible and laying the foundation for the EU.

questions.question: In 1978, China revolutionized agricultural productivity by replacing communal collective farming with which market-oriented reform system?
questions.explanation: The Household Responsibility System contracted collective farmland to individual families, allowing them to sell above-quota grain on local markets, sparking a massive boom in rural output.

questions.question: The historic Land Boundary Agreement that resolved the 70-year-old boundary dispute and exchanged 162 adverse enclaves between India and Bangladesh was ratified by the:
questions.explanation: The 100th Amendment Act of 2015 gave effect to the 1974 Land Boundary Agreement and 2011 protocol, transferring 111 enclaves to Bangladesh and 51 enclaves to India.

questions.question: The World Bank Group consists of five closely linked institutions. Which of the following is the private sector lending arm of the World Bank Group?
options: D) International Centre for Settlement of Investment Disputes (ICSID)
questions.explanation: The International Finance Corporation (IFC), established in 1956, promotes sustainable private sector investment in developing countries.

questions.question: In traditional realist security theory, a state can maintain or restore the 'Balance of Power' against a rising hegemon through two primary methods: 'Internal Balancing' and 'External Balancing'. 'Internal Balancing' involves:
options: A) Signing bilateral mutual defense pacts with third-party nations
B) Building domestic economic wealth, industrial capability, and national military forces
C) Surrendering sovereign defense policy to the United Nations General Assembly
D) Abolishing all intelligence agencies and armed border patrols
questions.explanation: Internal balancing relies on self-help (boosting economic output, defense budgets, weapons innovation), whereas external balancing relies on creating or joining military alliances.

questions.question: Principle 7 of the 1992 Rio Declaration on Environment and Development is celebrated in international law because it formally established the doctrine of:
questions.explanation: Principle 7 of the Rio Declaration states that in view of the different contributions to global environmental degradation, states have common but differentiated responsibilities.

questions.question: Political theorists observe that economic globalisation fosters the withdrawal of the state from welfare functions, returning state authority to the classical 'minimalist state' functions of:
options: A) Directing price controls on all consumer goods and farm seeds
B) Operating state monopolies over banking, transport, and communication
C) Providing guaranteed universal public housing for all citizens
D) Maintaining law and order and defending national territorial security
questions.explanation: Under neoliberal globalization, the state rolls back welfare interventions (health, education, food subsidies) and restricts its primary role to maintaining law, order, contracts, and defense.

questions.question: The accession of Junagadh to Pakistan in August 1947 was geographically and politically untenable because:
options: A) Junagadh was surrounded on three sides by Indian territory, and its own feudatory states (Babariawad and Mangrol) acceded to India, creating an impossible geographical patchwork.
B) Junagadh had zero coastline and was completely landlocked within the Himalayas.
C) The Nawab had signed a mutual defense pact with the United States Navy.
D) The United Nations Security Council had declared all princely states independent republics.
questions.explanation: Junagadh was surrounded by Indian states; its vassal chiefs of Babariawad and Mangrol declared accession to India. When the Nawab sent troops to occupy them, India intervened diplomatically and militarily.

questions.question: Following the Third Five Year Plan (1961-1966), India postponed the Fourth Plan and declared three consecutive 'Annual Plans' (1966-1969), colloquially called 'Plan Holidays', primarily due to:
options: A) The total abolition of the Planning Commission by the Supreme Court of India.
B) Severe economic dislocations caused by the 1962 and 1965 wars, consecutive devastating monsoon failures/droughts, and a severe balance of payments crisis.
C) A sudden massive national budget surplus that eliminated the need for state planning.
D) A binding directive issued by the United Nations Trusteeship Council.
questions.explanation: The strains of two wars (1962, 1965), severe droughts in 1965-66, inflation, and devaluation of the rupee forced planners to abandon five-year targeting for three Annual Plans (1966-1969).

questions.question: How did the Chinese construction of the western highway through Aksai Chin and subsequent military incursions in the late 1950s violate the 1954 Panchsheel agreement?
options: A) They violated the principle of mandatory military alliance against the Western powers.
B) They breached the commercial tariff ceilings established under the General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade.
C) They directly violated the first and second principles: 'Mutual respect for each other's territorial integrity and sovereignty' and 'Mutual non-aggression'.
D) They contradicted the compulsory language translation clauses in the bilateral trade treaty.
questions.explanation: By occupying territory claimed by India without prior diplomatic disclosure and asserting military control over Aksai Chin, China breached the core Panchsheel tenets of mutual respect for territorial integrity and non-aggression.

questions.topic: Challenge to and Restoration of Congress System
questions.question: Indira Gandhi's spectacular political triumph in the 1971 general election restructured the social base of the Congress by forging a direct, unmediated electoral coalition comprising:
options: A) Exclusive industrial corporate conglomerates and urban stockbrokers.
B) The traditional conservative landed aristocracy of the former princely states.
C) The combined military officer corps and civil service secretariats.
D) Disadvantaged groups — the landless poor, Dalits, adivasis, religious minorities, and women — bypassing the traditional intermediate caste-landlord vote banks of the Syndicate.
questions.explanation: Indira Gandhi's 'Garibi Hatao' bypassed traditional rural vote-bank intermediaries, building a direct vertical alliance with the poor, Dalits, Muslims, and women who voted directly for her leadership.

questions.question: The 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act of 1976 modified Article 74 of the Constitution regarding the relationship between the President and the Council of Ministers by explicitly stipulating that:
options: A) The President 'shall act in accordance with such advice' tendered by the Council of Ministers headed by the Prime Minister, making ministerial advice legally binding.
B) The President could unilaterally dismiss the Prime Minister without assigning any reason.
C) The Council of Ministers could be appointed only with the prior concurrence of the Chief Justice of India.
D) The President possessed an absolute veto over all ordinary and constitutional amendment bills.
questions.explanation: The 42nd Amendment made the advice of the Council of Ministers explicitly binding on the President ('shall act in accordance with such advice'). The 44th Amendment later added a proviso allowing the President to send advice back once for reconsideration.

questions.question: Clause 6 of the historic Assam Accord signed in August 1985 remains a centerpiece of regional political aspirations because it promises that:
options: A) The State of Assam shall maintain its own independent paramilitary armed border force.
B) Constitutional, legislative, and administrative safeguards shall be provided to protect, preserve, and promote the cultural, social, and linguistic identity of the Assamese people.
C) All non-Assamese citizens residing in Assam shall be denied the right to vote in local elections.
D) The Union Government shall dissolve the state legislature and convert Assam into a Union Territory.
questions.explanation: Clause 6 guarantees that constitutional and administrative safeguards will be instituted to protect the cultural, social, and linguistic heritage of the indigenous Assamese populace.

questions.question: The Union Government's August 1990 announcement implementing the Mandal Commission recommendations unleashed intense political turmoil across north India, most visibly symbolized by:
options: A) A general strike organized by the Armed Forces opposing recruitment quotas.
B) The resignation of all Supreme Court judges in protest against backward class reservations.
C) Widespread student agitations, bandhs, and tragic self-immolations (beginning with Rajeev Goswami at Delhi University) opposing the 27% quota.
D) The immediate withdrawal of all foreign embassies from the national capital.
questions.explanation: The decision triggered massive protests across university campuses in north India, with street blockades and self-immolation bids by anti-reservation students, causing sharp social polarization.

questions.question: The collapse of the Soviet Union in 1991 fundamentally restructured the international system by producing which three transformative geopolitical realities?
options: A) The immediate formation of a single global military empire governed by the Warsaw Pact.
B) The total elimination of capitalism in Western Europe and the adoption of Gosplan planning in America.
C) The dissolution of the United Nations Security Council and the abolition of all sovereign borders.
D) The end of Cold War ideological confrontations, the emergence of a unipolar global order dominated by the United States, and the birth of fifteen sovereign successor states across Eurasia.
questions.explanation: The collapse ended the ideological battle between capitalism and communism, left the US as the preeminent superpower (unipolarity), and created 15 independent nations (Russia, Ukraine, Central Asian republics, etc.).

questions.question: In international relations theory, Joseph Nye analyzes hegemony through three distinct 'Faces of Power'. Which of the following accurately describes these three faces?
options: A) Nuclear power, solar power, and hydroelectric power.
B) Command power through military coercion (Hard Power), inducements through economic leverage, and co-optive power through cultural and ideological attraction (Soft Power).
C) Legislative power, judicial power, and monarchical power.
D) Naval power, infantry power, and orbital satellite power exclusively.
questions.explanation: Nye differentiates command power (military coercion), economic power (inducements and sanctions), and co-optive/soft power (shaping preferences through values, institutions, and culture).

questions.question: The compliance mechanism of the 1997 Kyoto Protocol was designed with a dual-branch structure to ensure accountability among Annex I countries. These two branches are the:
options: A) Military Intervention Branch and Naval Blockade Branch
B) Universal Taxation Branch and Trade Embargo Branch
C) Facilitative Branch (providing advice and financial assistance) and Enforcement Branch (determining non-compliance and applying penalties)
D) Judicial Extradition Branch and Sovereign Bankruptcy Branch
questions.explanation: The Kyoto Compliance Committee consists of the Facilitative Branch (assisting countries in meeting targets) and the Enforcement Branch (applying penalties, such as requiring 1.3 times the emissions shortfall in the next period).
